scope.environment: Local native C++ compiled with c++ -O2 -std=c++20; Linux sandbox, production build and integration runs were performed separately by the main agent and are not counted as this review's executions.

bindings.displayBinding: Editorial solution code exactly equals the frozen reference. Batch authoredSolutions and editorial exactly equal the corresponding editorial artifact.

source.provenance: The retrieved original screenshots supplement the fixed raw source; they are not asserted to be blobs from the fixed commit. Both describe clockwise quadrant rotation with both diagonals fixed. The first shows the original 5-by-5 matrix with highlighted diagonals, not an after-rotation illustration.
source.originalExampleVerified: The fixed source's 5-by-5 output matches the independently computed clockwise off-diagonal coordinate mapping; all 25 output values were checked.

domainAndProof.sourceLimits: No numeric n bound is stated in the original. Positive n, signed 32-bit matrix entries and nonnegative signed 32-bit turns are disclosed interface adaptations; no empty-matrix extension is used.
domainAndProof.mapping: For an off-diagonal source coordinate (r,c), one turn maps to (c,n-1-r). Both diagonal sets are invariant under this rotation, so keeping their values fixed never conflicts with an off-diagonal orbit. Every off-diagonal orbit has four members; the strict top triangle used by the reference visits each orbit once.
domainAndProof.independentInverseMapping: For destination (r,c), diagonal values are unchanged. For turns modulo 4 equal to 1,2,3, the independent oracle reads source (n-1-c,r), (n-1-r,n-1-c), (c,n-1-r), respectively. It does not simulate the reference's in-place four-cycle updates.
domainAndProof.boundaryCoverage: Odd/even n, n=1 and n=2, center and both diagonals, turns 0/1/2/3/4/INT_MAX, negative matrix values including INT_MIN and INT_MAX, CRLF parsing, and full-size EOF input are covered. Coordinate R^4 identity was also checked on every small case.
domainAndProof.capacity: With one-digit entries, one-digit turns and EOF, minimum input bytes are 2*n*n + digits(n) + 2. n=4095 needs 33,538,056 bytes; n=4096 needs 33,554,438, exceeding the existing 33,554,432-byte input budget. Thus 4095 follows from transport capacity, not an invented source bound.
domainAndProof.resources: At n=4095 the single int32 matrix occupies 67,076,100 bytes. At most three in-place turns give O(n^2) time and O(n^2) storage, without recursion or a second matrix. Output preserves the multiset of signed values and remains within the configured output budget.

reproducibility.executionPolicy: Cases processed sequentially; compact independent input array released before launching each reference or mutant. No author generator or upstream solution was read or executed. Only this review report was added inside the repository.
